A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EEPO research. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original mathematical-reasoning experiments across three models, including benchmark scores, exploration analyses, training dynamics, and computational efficiency.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds Qwen3-14B-Base results and evaluations combining EEPO with other exploration settings in Appendices C–D.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 changes probability stabilization from two-sided clipping to an upper cap in Equation 8 and reverses the stabilized loss sign in Equation 9. The two-stage rollout, entropy gate, and temporary update remain unchanged. Inconsistent signs elsewhere prevent interpreting this as a clearly established reversal of the implemented update.

E1.justification: Both versions train on MATH and evaluate on Minerva Math, OlympiadBench, AMC 2023, AIME 2024, and AIME 2025. The added experiments extend model configurations and combinations on existing tasks, without adding datasets or distinct test scenarios.

E2.justification: The evaluated baseline set remains the untrained models, GRPO, and its higher-temperature, increased-entropy, DAPO clip-higher, and more-rollouts variants. Tables 4–5 reuse existing GRPO comparators; the new configurations are EEPO-enhanced variants rather than additional competing algorithms.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds evaluation with Qwen3-14B-Base, and Appendix D adds configurations combining EEPO with increased entropy or clip higher. Existing training and evaluation settings are otherwise retained. Section 4.1 corrects Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct to Qwen3-8B-Base, already identified in v1's Table 3 and Appendix A, so this does not establish a replacement experiment.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a controlled comparison addressing whether EEPO provides benefits alongside entropy regularization and clip higher. Appendix C adds evidence about applicability at a larger model size. Existing hyperparameter sensitivity, exploration dynamics, Pass@k, and efficiency analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added appendix results retain single-value reporting without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports Qwen3-14B-Base averages of 40.6 for GRPO and 44.7 for EEPO. Table 5 adds EEPO-plus-entropy accuracy of 27.9 versus 23.9 for its GRPO counterpart, and EEPO-plus-clip-higher accuracy of 26.6 versus 22.9. Original results remain unchanged apart from equivalent rounding of 35.22 to 35.2 in Table 3.

T1.justification: Equations 8–9 revise the mathematical definitions of clipping and stabilized complementary loss. These are substantive formula changes, but no theorem, proof, or new derivation is added. Equation 10 retains the positive-log objective, while Equation 11 and Algorithm 1 retain opposing update signs, leaving the mathematical specification inconsistent.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same sample-then-forget contribution, exploration and efficiency claims, and headline relative gains of 24.3%, 33.0%, and 10.4%. New appendix evidence does not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly interprets the larger-model results as showing effectiveness across the 3B–14B range, particularly on challenging AIME benchmarks. Existing explanations of entropy collapse, generalization, and efficiency remain unchanged, and no substantive limitations analysis is added.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly identifies 16 rollouts as the more-rollouts baseline's default; this value was already among v1's tested settings. Appendix A removes the disclosure that Pass@k uses temperature 1.0, without establishing a changed procedure. The main model list is corrected, while hardware information and code-access promises remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6 revises its RLVR overview and adds six references, including PEARL, REVEAL, and Co-reward, while removing the Chen 2021 code-model evaluation and Cobbe 2021 verifier references. EEPO's positioning relative to objective-level exploration methods and knowledge-erasure unlearning remains intact.

P1.justification: Changes include a localized related-work rewrite, expanded baseline explanations, reorganized appendices and disclosures, acknowledgments, and updated affiliation and conference-header text. The LLM-use disclosure is shortened and names GPT-5. Most main-text language and section structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4–5, removes highlighted relative-gain annotations from Tables 1–3, and relocates Figure 6 from page 8 to page 9. The eight existing figures retain their content. Other changes concern table spacing, headers, and page flow.

improvement.justification: Tables 4–5 provide useful additional evidence for larger-model applicability and compatibility with existing exploration settings, and the model-name correction improves consistency. These are limited gains: the new experiments have sparse setup details, the Pass@k temperature disclosure is lost, and the revised loss equations remain inconsistent with the update specification. The added empirical support nevertheless provides a modest overall improvement.
